messages:
sara_support: Hey team, ACME reported that their monthly credits hit 0 and they expected a refill at 10:00 UTC but API 429s continued until ~10:25 UTC. Tenant: tenant-acme-prod, timezone America/Los_Angeles. Customer is seeing this intermittently across long-running sessions. Can someone confirm how the refill job interacts with the caching layer?

acme_csm: Repro steps from the customer: 1) heavy long-polling inference for 2 hours, 2) credits drop to 0 at 09:58 PDT, 3) at 10:00 PDT UI shows credits refilled but API still returns 429 for ~20m. They provided a curl trace and the app logs (attached).

mike_billing: Looking. Two quick things: did they have a promo/topup applied? that can affect visible vs. backend buckets. Also want the refill job run logs for 10:00 UTC.

infra-bot: [alert] refill-runner-03 failed to acquire lock at 2024-11-14T10:00:05Z, fallback retry succeeded at 2024-11-14T10:06:12Z (duration 6m7s). error: redis/lock-timeout.

dan_ops: That alert explains it — lock acquisition delay pushed the middle step. Short summary of our refill path: billing service writes new token allocation to postgres, then invalidates tenant cache in redis, then API cache-traces allow requests through. If lock delayed, API may still read stale zero from cache until TTL expires or invalidation runs.

mike_billing: Can you paste the relevant log snippet and the redis TTL for tenant-acme-prod? we need to know if invalidation fired before the retry.

acme_csm: Copied from customer logs: "GET /v1/usage -> 429, X-Account: tenant-acme-prod, time: 2024-11-14T10:03:12Z". They also included an internal trace showing a cache hit on key credits:tenant-acme-prod with TTL 180s at 10:02:59Z.

dan_ops: TTL 180s explains 20m gap (well, 3m TTL — but combined with lock delay and request spikes it can look like longer because of aggressive in-flight retries). Quick repro command to inspect current cached value (run on staging infra):
```
redis-cli -h redis-primary get credits:tenant-acme-prod
redis-cli -h redis-primary ttl credits:tenant-acme-prod
```
Run that and share output.

mike_billing: Also run this internal billing API check to confirm authoritative state:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" "https://billing.internal/api/v1/tenants/tenant-acme-prod/credits" | jq
```
We want the backend number vs cache number.

acme_csm: I ran the billing check with customer-provided logs: billing shows 50000 tokens allocated at 10:00:01Z. redis get returned "0" at 10:02:59Z, ttl 175. So we did write backend but cache was stale for a window. Customer retried rapidly and hit 429s while cache TTL hadn't expired.

sara_support: Thanks — that aligns. Customer upset because UI showed refill immediately while API stayed 429. Is there a recommended mitigation we can offer them now?

dan_ops: Short-term: ask them to restart long-running connections or re-open sessions after refill; that forces a fresh read. Longer-term: we should make the refill path invalidate cache synchronously (or publish a pub/sub notification) so API reads fresh data.

mike_billing: I'll propose a patch: after the postgres write, publish tenant id to credits-invalidation topic and have API workers subscribe to invalidate local caches immediately. This should cut the observed window to <1s. I'll file a PR.

acme_csm: For now I offered ACME a manual top-up to cover the 20m outage and asked them to restart their streaming clients. They accepted top-up.

dan_ops: Follow-ups: 1) engineering to track PR to implement pub/sub invalidation (owner: mike_billing), 2) add extra telemetry: record lock acquisition time and cache invalidation lag per refill run (owner: dan_ops), 3) run a postmortem if this repeats.

sara_support: Escalating to billing-eng. @mike_billing can you add ETA for the PR and the priority? customer has SLA credit in play.

mike_billing: ETA: small spike fix -> branch + tests by EOD tomorrow, roll to canary within 48h. Prioritizing as P2 -> P1 if we see recurrence.

infra-bot: [note] created incident INC-2024-1189 for refill-lock-delay and linked to ticket AP-3492.

acme_csm: Customer updated: accepted the temporary top-up and will restart their sessions. They'll monitor and reopen if they see any more 429s. :thumbsup:

sara_support: Great — leaving notes on the ticket and will close once PR is in review and top-up applied. Thanks everyone.
